prompt:
A blank, empty trading-card frame template for a card game based on the War in Heaven, the fall of the rebel angels and the Apocalypse, seen perfectly flat and straight-on, filling the whole image edge to edge, portrait orientation. Layout from top to bottom: a narrow horizontal title bar across the top with a round empty medallion at its right end; below it a large rectangular art window taking up about the upper half of the card, filled with solid flat pure black (#000000) with crisp straight edges; below that a thin horizontal type bar; below that a large empty rectangular text box of pale aged parchment; at the bottom right a small empty plaque overlapping the corner of the text box. The title bar, medallion, type bar, text box and plaque are completely blank. Style: a rustic, retro 1990s hand-painted trading-card frame, gouache and ink texture, worn and weathered like an old printed card, muted colours, matte with no glossy highlights, no glow, no light rays, no sky, symmetrical with clean edges. Absolutely no text, no letters, no numbers, no symbols, no logo, no watermark, and nothing inside the black window.

Legendary rarity, the most epic frame of all: the great red dragon of the Apocalypse, with seven crowned heads and ten horns, coiled all the way around the card in blazing gold and crimson scales, its heads rearing over the top edge, its tail sweeping a third of the stars from the sky along one side; a burning halo of golden light behind the art window, gold leaf everywhere, fire and falling stars. Colours: blazing gold and deep crimson on black. Overwhelming and climactic, still hand-painted, never glossy or 3D-rendered. IMPORTANT: the border is exactly as thin as on an ordinary card frame, so the art window and the text box are just as large as on the other rarities: the dragon's body is drawn slim and tight along the outer edges only, and its seven heads are small, kept inside the thin band above the title bar; nothing pushes the title bar, art window or text box inwards or downwards. The look of a medieval illuminated Apocalypse manuscript (like the Beatus and Angers Apocalypse): gold leaf, deep ultramarine, vermilion and black; flames, falling stars, scorched angel feathers and broken halos; dark and ominous, the host of the fallen. No Greek, Norse, Chinese or Egyptian elements.
Near-mint condition: aged and antique, but no play wear, creases or scuffs. The wear is on the frame only; the black art window stays solid, untouched black.
